record: Places and roads on the real map: build step 1 of docs/COLONIES.md
verdictMeaning: The settlements, Gonzales's ford and Castañeda's camp, and 26 roads stand on the real terrain; no road crosses a big river except at a crossing on it; every town is reachable from Gonzales by road; a class made on this map places its families near Gonzales, plays the Gonzales chapter to its documented end, and survives save and reload. Classes made without the option are unchanged.

build.output: public/terrain/colonies-map.json.gz: 23 places, 26 roads, 418 watercourses, 0.52 MB JSON
dataLessons: A river's line breaks at modern dams (Guadalupe at New Braunfels, Colorado at Austin): the bank check first found Gonzales on Béxar's side. Loose ends within a mile are joined.
A river entering from beyond the map starts half a mile inside its edge: carried to the edge.

The elevation has bays at sea level, not as no-data: the land could be walked round the Guadalupe's mouth across San Antonio Bay. Under a metre is water for the bank check; under 30 cm for roads, which otherwise could not reach the low coastal prairie; the sea is cleared round coastal towns such as Velasco.
The Colorado at Matagorda is drawn as two channels half a mile apart: the road to Victoria went 162 miles round by Columbus until crossings opened 0.6 miles.
NHD heights at an eighth of a mile cannot tell upstream from downstream; the walk to the camp follows the flowlines' own digitising direction.

roadsAddedOnEvidence: Matagorda to Victoria through the Lavaca country: without it Matagorda was 198 road miles from Gonzales for 105 as the crow flies; Matagorda's volunteers were sent west to Kerr's on the Lavaca (HIST-TEX-006).
Mina to Gonzales: without it Mina was 183 road miles for 43; Colorado men fought at Gonzales (HIST-TEX-007).
worlds: Colonies worlds built for 5, 10, 15, 20 and 30 families over 20 seeds each: 100 of 100, 3.6 s in all. A first version failed where a house stood in a bend of the Guadalupe with no road reachable without crossing it, and where rounding moved a house across a bend; placement now refuses such spots at the stored position.

liveBrowserProof.note: Same computer only. MAP=colonies PORT=8753 SEED=colonies-proof PLAYERS=5; one student in the browser pane. The pane was 280 x 235, so the map canvas was enlarged off-screen and its crops shown filling the pane for screenshots.
observed: The page loaded the class with map.source texas-colonies-map and 32 sites, and no fault.
At about 200 pixels a mile: the real meandering Guadalupe and San Marcos, roads, the town and homesteads drawn.

Zoomed out (about 73 pixels a mile): the rivers first drew as broad blue bands, the meanders running together; fixed to near true width on the real map, after which thin meandering rivers with timber along them and the roads between settlements drew.
A later close-up capture did not refresh and is not relied on.
